q-6409.name: Question 1
q-6409.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249653/assets/43a50373c9cfa5925a01054ab5eb465ac8a6220fced41ab46d8e026908884537.png)

Calculate the length of the side $x$, giving your answer to two decimal places.
q-6409.worked_solution:
The Law of Cosines states that

$$
{x}^{2}={y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2yz\operatorname{cos}⁡X.
$$

Here, we have

$$
m∠X={66}^{∘},\,y=16,\,z=19.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & ={16}^{2}+{19}^{2}-2(16)(19)\operatorname{cos}⁡{66}^{∘} \\  & =256+361-608\operatorname{cos}⁡{66}^{∘} \\  & =617-608(0.406\,73…) \\  & =617-247.295\,88 \\  & =369.704\,12\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places

Taking the square root gives

$$
x=\sqrt{369.708\,16}=19.23
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

q-14692.name: Question 2
q-14692.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249653/assets/66d24d8cc70ffaed2421d0a5a0086fd7848b4d3e98bc8a6e87588c6c2b04e19d.png)

Calculate the length of the side $c$, giving your answer to two decimal places.
q-14692.worked_solution:
The Law of Cosines states that

$$
{c}^{2}={a}^{2}+{b}^{2}-2ab\operatorname{cos}⁡C.
$$

Here, we have

$$
m∠C={43}^{∘},\,a=10,\,b=13.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={10}^{2}+{13}^{2}-2(10)(13)\operatorname{cos}⁡{43}^{∘} \\  & =100+169-260\operatorname{cos}⁡{43}^{∘} \\  & =269-260(0.731\,35…) \\  & =269-190.151\,96 \\  & =78.848\,04.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places

Taking the square root gives

$$
c=\sqrt{78.848\,04}=8.88
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

q-201.name: Question 3
q-201.problem: A triangle has sides $a$, $b$, and $c.$ The sides $a$, $b$, and $c$ are of lengths  $9$, $12$, and $18$, respectively. What is the measure of the angle between the sides $b$ and $c?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
q-201.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249653/assets/dede0326d992509dedf1c3a2854b47076ccc48ebf0e07705c8c12762d8ecdead.png)

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A & =\frac{{b}^{2}+{c}^{2}-{a}^{2}}{2bc}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Here, we have

$$
a=9,\,b=12,\,c=18.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A & =\frac{{12}^{2}+{18}^{2}-{9}^{2}}{2(12)(18)} \\  & =\frac{144+324-81}{432} \\  & =\frac{387}{432}\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠F & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{387}{432}) \\  & ={26.38}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

q-201.html:
Question 3
?

A triangle has sides a, b, and c. The sides a, b, and c are of lengths 9, 12, and 18, respectively. What is the measure of the angle between the sides b and c? Round your answer to two decimal places.

a
27.42∘
b
23.62∘
c
29.38∘
d
26.38∘
e
20.73∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The following triangle illustrates the information given.

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle A: cos⁡A=b2+c2−a22bc.

Here, we have a=9,b=12,c=18.

This gives cos⁡A=122+182−922(12)(18)=144+324−81432=387432 Therefore, m∠F=arccos⁡(387432)=26.38∘ rounded to two decimal places.

For the triangle above, find $m∠A$ in degrees to two decimal places.
q-14701.worked_solution:
We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A=\frac{{b}^{2}+{c}^{2}-{a}^{2}}{2bc}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have

$$
a=5,\,b=8,\,c=9.
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡A & =\frac{{9}^{2}+{8}^{2}-{5}^{2}}{2(9)(8)} \\  & =\frac{81+64-25}{144} \\  & =\frac{120}{144} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{5}{6}) \\  & ={33.56}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
